text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Stockholm's Mayor Mats Hulth has come out against a report that said the profits from Stockholm hosting the 2004 Olympic Games would not be as large as spokesmen for the campaign have claimed. Hulth said why start criticising when it was only two weeks away from the decision on who wins the games.

- The newspaper Arbetet Nyheterna is facing an acute crisis, needing 8.2 million crowns to survive, but the umbrella union group, LO, is refusing to fund the paper out of its trouble. A merger with Skanska Dagbladet could be the only way out of its economic dilemma.

- The better than expected growth in forestry in the first quarter of the year strengthened further in the second quarter. Forestry companies are signalling larger volumes and say the stronger U.S. dollar and higher pulp prices will help their performance for the rest of 1997.
- The National Debt Office wants to change the way that the state's debt is funded with more loans in Swedish crowns aided by government bonds and less in foreign currencies.

- Ericsson has proposed a six billion crown programme of convertible debentures for its staff. With the fast growing mobile telephone business, Ericsson needs still more money so it borrrowing from its employees.

- Property company Diligentia held fast to its forecast of a half year result of less than 200 million crowns, posting a profit after financial items of 147 million crowns. The acquisition of Hufvudstaden International, if it goes through, will only have a marginal effect on 1997 results.
- Sweden's state-owned power company Vattenfall has again offered to buy all shares in Finland's Savon Voima. It made a bid worth 1.3 billion crowns that is open until the middle of September.

- Swedish forestry firm SCA said it will move the headquarters of its hygiene operations, including its large and profitable Monlycke subsidiary, to Munich in Germany. The move is in connection with SCA's 2.4 billion crowns bid on the rest of the shares in German company PWA .

- Tax collectors impounded about 200,000 crowns worth of apparently fake Callaway golf clubs from a store called Sport & Golf in central Stockholm. Callaway is the Californian producer of golf clubs including the world-famous Big Bertha.
- Forestry company MoDo reported pre-tax profit for the first half fell to 526 million crowns against 803 million a year ago. This sum included a loss of 294 million crowns from currency hedging.

-- Nordbanken, Sweden's fourth largest bank, posted a 17 percent drop in second quarter profit as costs rose and margins on lending fell. The bank reported that net earnings in the first half of the year declined by 15 percent to 2.3 billion crowns.
